originalTitle: Commonwealth Games 2026: England beat South Africa in netball, athletics, track cycling on day seven – as it happened
summary: England qualified for the netball semi-finals with the final act of an intriguing day, while the women’s 1500m wheelchair race will be restaged
content: That was a real nail-biter. England were were 17-11 down after Q1. Some fightback there. And with that I’ll sign off. Thanks for joining and please come back tomorrow for more Games joy and medals. England hold on. The relief is palpable and the emotions raw. The Roses go through to play New Zealand in the semi-final on Saturday. Netball: England 56-52 South Africa Down to the final two minutes in the match and it’s slipping away from South Africa now. England are on the verge of the semi-finals. Can they see it home? Netball: England 54-50 South Africa Five minutes to play in the final quarter and it’s tightened up again. Netball: England 41-34 South Africa Just under four minutes to play in quarter three. Netball: England 36-32 South Africa Still a long way to go, over 20 minutes, but this is some fightback from England. Since the start of the second quarter they lead 26-15. Athletics: Women’s 100m hurdles final Devynne Charlton, who won silver in 2022, goes one better this time. She started superbly, led for pretty much the entire race and finished comfortably clear of Megan Simmonds. The defending champion Tobi Amusan had a bad start and never recovered. Netball: England 32-30 South Africa England have edged in front at the start of the third quarter. I think this might be the first time they’ve been ahead in the match. Athletics The women’s discus has been won emphatically by Jamaica’s Samantha Hall with a best throw of 61.66m. Women’s 5000m final Rose Davies won gold ahead of her fellow Australian Jessica Hull; there were just eight-hundredths of a second between them. Scotland’s Megan Keith took bronze and is high on life as she chats to the TNT Sports team. Half time: England 28-29 South Africa England are right back in it after dominating the second quarter at the Hydro. It’s literally too close to call. Netball: England 23-24 South Africa England are having a superb second quarter and have reduced the deficit to one. I should have said that, if this does end in a draw, England will go through by virtue of their superior goal average. Imogen Allison also seems okay after that injury scare a few minutes ago. Weightlifting Another plug for Sean Ingle’s excellent piece on Emily Campbell’s gold earlier today. Netball: England 17-20 South Africa England have closed the gap to three but they’ve lost Imogen Allison to a potential ankle injury. Netball: England 11-17 South Africa A terrific start for South Africa, who have a handy lead at the end of the first quarter. There isn’t much in it but they’ve been sharper in a few key moments. Netball: England 4-4 South Africa It’s all square with just over 10 minutes left in the first quarter. Netball The crunch match between England and South Africa is under way in The Hydro. These are the starting line-ups. England Tchine, Pearson, Shaw, Carter, Allison, Williams, Pechova. South Africa Chawane, Mathe, Ngubane, Smith, Van den Berg, Van Wyk, Visser. Athletics: Men’s 800m semi-final The English pair of Alex Botterill and Ben Pattinson have qualified for tomorrow’s final, but Wales’ Justin Davies missed out by nine-hundredths of a second. Athletics Thea LaFond of Dominica extended her lead in the triple jump with a winning leap of 14.60m. The Jamaican pair of Ackelia Smith (14.04) and Shantae Foreman (13.96) took silver and bronze. Athletics The men’s shot put has been won by Chukwuebuka Enekwechi of Nigeria. He threw 21.07m to finish just in front of Tom Walsh (21.03m) and Scott Lincoln (20.99m) Weightlifting: Men’s +110kg final New Zealand’s David Liti has won the gold in this one. He lifted 223kg in the clean & jerk to take gold with one attempt to spare. Gold David Liti (New Zealand) 389 Silver Lovepreet Singh (India) 388 Bronze Andrew Griffiths (England) 356 It’s been a night to remember for Andrew Griffiths, who probably wasn’t fancied for a medal at the start. Athletics The mighty Adaejah Hodge of the British Virgin Islands has broken the Commonwealth Games record in the 200m semi-finals. She eased to victory in a cracking time of 22.01. The British champions Success Eduan made it through to tomorrow’s final as one of the fastest runners to finish outside the first two in their individual semi-final. Netball: England v South Africa (9pm) There’s a huge game coming up in the hydro tonight. England and South Africa meet in what is effectively a quarter-final. The winners will go through in second place in Pool A, with New Zealand waiting in Saturday’s semi-final. The pool winners Australia beat Northern Ireland 88-27 earlier in the day. They finish with five wins from five and will play Jamaica in the semi-finals. Weightlifting: Men’s +110kg final Lovepreet Singh of India has stormed past Andrew Griffiths and into the lead after lifting an eye-watering 205kg with his first attempt in the clean & jerk. Weightlifting: Men’s +110kg final The Englishman Andrew Griffiths his lifted 191kg with his second attempat the clean & jerk, which gives him an overall lead of 20kg as I type. Athletics Dominica’s Theo LaFond has a huge lead at the halfway mark in the women’s triple jump final. She has jumped 14.59, with Ackelia Smith currently second on 14.00. The women’s 100m T47 final was won by the Canadian Sheriauna Haase in a time of 12.23. England’s Zac Shaw storms to victory in the men’s 100m T12 final, clocking a time of 10.89. That’s the fulfilment of a long-standing dream for Shaw, who took silver four years ago, and he’s full of emotion as he celebrates in the Glasgow evening sun. By the time Emily Campbell stepped on to the platform for a final time on Thursday, the women’s +86kg weightlifting final had all the fervour of a revivalist meeting. Everyone was cheering. There were loud shouts and exhortations. And people who didn’t know a snatch from a clean and jerk two hours before had become instant converts. It was the Campbell Effect in action again.
